text: . The Government has said that 60 merchant vessels carrying cargo were safely moved through the Strait of Hormuz despite the heightened security situation in the West Asia region. Replying to a question in Parliament, the government also disclosed that 3,972 Indian seafarers were repatriated from the Gulf region, while a round-the-clock crisis management system handled tens of thousands of distress calls and emails.The government’s response highlights India’s maritime response during the ongoing West Asia crisis, underscoring how New Delhi managed to keep one of the country’s most critical trade arteries functioning even as tensions threatened shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The strategic waterway connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, and serves as the world’s most critical maritime chokepoint for energy supplies.

. India has termed the so-called local elections in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir a complete farce, saying such hollow exercises cannot hide reality. Briefing media in New Delhi, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal pointed out that the real happening is that of public protests and wanton killings by Pakistani forces.He said that since June this year, at least 90 civilians have lost their lives in the continuing crackdown. He said that the Pakistani establishment has answered public discontent with bullets, black outs, intimidation and repression and now seeks to manufacture legitimacy through a hollow electoral exercise. He added that Pakistan must be held accountable and the world should see through Pakistan’s hypocritical lecturing on human rights.Replying to a query on invitation for BRICS Summit to be held in Delhi in September, Mr Jaiswal said a formal invitation for a bilateral visit to India was extended to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman upon his assumption of office in February this year.He informed that as far as the BRICS Summit is concerned, India has separately extended an invitation to Bangladesh Prime Minister in his capacity as the current Chair of BIMSTEC to attend the outreach session of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi. He added that the invitation has been extended as per the standard practice being followed in BRICS for the outreach sessions. Other heads of regional groups have also been invited in a similar manner.On a media interaction by former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, the spokesperson said that the interaction is being organised by a private media entity. He said the government has no involvement in it and neither does it endorse any views that may be expressed at the forum.

. Qatar’s Foreign Ministry says diplomatic efforts are intensifying to find a solution to the ongoing US-Iran conflict, with regional mediators working closely to facilitate negotiations and exchange proposals between the two sides. It said Qatar is actively supporting Oman’s mediation efforts and remains optimistic that an agreement could be reached within the coming hours or days.While confirming that no direct talks are taking place between Washington and Tehran, officials said mediators continue to relay messages and circulate draft agreements between the parties, a process that has been underway since the conflict escalated in February.Meanwhile, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent today expressed optimism that progress could come quickly, saying Washington could secure a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as early as “today or tomorrow.”Tensions in the region remain high as British maritime monitoring agency reported that a cargo ship was struck by an unknown projectile overnight while sailing through the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one crew member missing.The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations centre said the incident occurred when the vessel was about 23 miles northeast of Al Khasab, Oman.

. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has projected GDP growth to 6.7 percent in this fiscal year, deciding to keep the Repo rate unchanged at 5.25 percent with neutral stance. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said that country’s economic growth continues to be supported by resilient demand and it remains world’s fastest growing large economy. He said, country’s economy has performed better than expected in April-June quarter of this fiscal year.Announcing the Monetary Policy Committee’s decision today, Mr. Malhotra said, RBI has decided to keep repo rate unchanged at 5.25 percent and retained a neutral stance. Repo rate is the interest rate at which the central bank lends short-term money to commercial banks against government securities.He said, RBI has lowered CPI inflation projection to 5 percent from earlier estimate of 5.1 percent for financial year 2027. The Governor said the recent rise in inflation was largely driven by food and fuel prices rather than broad-based demand pressures.Mr. Malhotra said, economy had performed better than expected during the first quarter of the financial year, prompting the central bank to revise its real GDP growth projection for 2026-27 to 6.7 per cent. The RBI Governor said, West Asia conflict continues to challenge global economy by disrupting key trade routes.RBI struck an optimistic note on the domestic economy, raising its growth projection for 2026-27 while lowering its inflation forecast, saying robust exports, steady investment activity and easing supply-side disruptions have strengthened the macroeconomic outlook despite persistent global uncertainties.On the external front, the RBI said foreign direct investment inflows remained robust while foreign portfolio investment has witnessed a turnaround in recent months. The Governor said, country’s foreign exchange reserves remain comfortable at nearly 693 billion US dollars, providing import cover of more than ten months.RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra has said that Polymer notes are expected to be in circulation at the beginning of next financial year, if everything goes as per schedule. Addressing a press conference in Mumbai, Mr. Malhotra said, Polymer notes enhances durability. He said that details about the security features and other will be communicated soon. While talking about Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) and Unified Lending Interface, Deputy Governor Rohit Jain said that its uses is increasing and various stakeholders are accepting it.

. In the Lok Sabha, the Taxation and Other Laws ( Amendment) Bill, 2026 is listed for consideration and passing in today’s business of the House. The Bill seeks to amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the Income-tax Act, 2025, and the Finance Act, 2026.In the Rajya Sabha, the Appropriation (No.3) Bill, 2026 is listed in the business of the House for consideration and return. The legislation provides for the authorisation of appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the amounts spent on certain services during the financial year ended on the 31st of March, 2023, in excess of the amounts granted for those services and for that year. The Lok Sabha has already given its approval to the Bill.

. The Government has extended the tenure of Dr. T.V. Somanathan as the Cabinet Secretary by one year. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) has approved the one-year extension in the service of Dr. T.V. Somanathan, as Cabinet Secretary beyond 30 August 2026.The ACC has also approved the tenure extension of Govind Mohan as the Home Secretary by one year.

. India enjoyed a mixed day at the Korea Masters Badminton tournament in Asan, with seven women’s singles players advancing to the second round, while all six Indian men’s singles shuttlers crashed out in the opening round.In the women’s singles, Anmol Kharb, Mansi Singh, Rakshitha Ramraj, Ashmita Chaliha, Isharani Baruah, Tanvi Sharma and Shriyanshi Valishetty progressed to the second round with impressive victories.Anmol Kharb defeated Hong Kong China’s Lo Sin Yan 16-21, 21-17, 21-12, while Mansi Singh came from behind to beat Korea’s Kim Joo Eun 14-21, 21-19, 21-9. Rakshitha Ramraj overcame Korea’s A Yeon Yoo 22-24, 21-12, 21-13 and Ashmita Chaliha defeated Japan’s Ririna Hiramoto 22-20, 21-18.Isharani Baruah beat Korea’s Lee So Hee 18-21, 21-15, 21-7, while Tanvi Sharma defeated China’s An Qi Yuan 21-16, 21-15. Shriyanshi Valishetty also advanced after defeating Chinese Taipei’s Yu Po Pai 21-15, 21-14. However, Aakarshi Kashyap bowed out after losing to Korea’s Min Ji Kim in the round of 32.In the women’s doubles, Sonali Singh and Ritika Thaker entered the second round with a win over Korea’s Ji Sun Bang and Hyun Ji Jang.In the mixed doubles, sixth seeds Shruti Mishra and Ishaan Bhatnagar defeated fellow Indians Sathwik Reddy Kanapuram and Radhika Sharma to move into the next round.In the men’s singles, former world number one Kidambi Srikanth, Mithun Manjunath, Kiran George, Rounak Chouhan, Saneeth Dayanand and Tharun Mannepalli all suffered first-round defeats.In the men’s doubles, the unseeded Indian pair of Krishna Prasad Garaga and Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy caused an upset by defeating sixth seeds Chaloempon Charoenkitamorn and Worrapol Thongsa-Nga of Thailand 21-16, 21-18 to reach the second round yesterday. They will now face the Korean pair of Y Kim and T Shin in the Pre-Quarterfinals tomorrow.

. An Indian-flagged commercial vessel, MSV Faize Noore Oliya, sank in the Red Sea after coming under attack off the coast of Yemen yesterday. All the 14 seafarers, including 13 Indian nationals, who were on board the vessel were rescued safely. According to reports, the Indian-flagged tanker was carrying oil from Saudi Arabia.Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal said that the vessel was hit by a projectile near Yemeni waters, causing the vessel to capsize and sink. Mr Sonowal said, India strongly condemns this unprovoked attack on the defenceless mechanised sailing vessel. He said, the safety of our people is our supreme priority.In a statement, Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) condemned the attack on the Indian-flagged vessel, saying the continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply worrisome. It said the targeting of commercial shipping in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region must be restored at the earliest.The Ministry said that the Indian Embassy in Riyadh is closely monitoring the situation and proactively coordinating with Yemeni authorities for the safety and security of the crew.

. The countdown to the 2030 Ahmedabad Commonwealth Games has officially begun, with the curtain falling on the Glasgow Commonwealth Games last night. As the curtain came down, India offered the world a vibrant invitation to Ahmedabad, blending ancient philosophy, contemporary artistry and cultural grandeur in a handover presentation that officially launched the journey towards the centenary edition of the Games in 2030.Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh, representing King Charles III, formally declared the Games closed in Glasgow. He called up on athletes of all countries and territories to visit Ahmedabad in four years’ time to celebrate the 24th Commonwealth Games.The formal handover began with the Commonwealth Games flag making its symbolic journey across the arena. Led by bearers holding the Scottish and Indian flags, the procession lowered the folded Games flag. Glasgow’s Lord Provost Jacqueline McLaren then passed it to Commonwealth Games Scotland vice-chair Susan Jackson, two-time Olympic medallist Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, and finally Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi.This marked the official transfer of hosting responsibilities from Scotland to India. India last hosted the Commonwealth Games in New Delhi in 2010. After 11 days of intense competition, Indian athletes departed from Glasgow as a satisfied bunch after winning 39 medals at the 2026 Games, including 13 gold, 17 silver, and nine bronze, to end in fourth position on the standings.

. Pakistan has tightened its control over foreign media by introducing new rules that require foreign journalists to obtain prior government approval before reporting from most parts of the country. Pakistan is under international scrutiny over its handling of protests and crackdown in Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir (POJK), where human rights groups and press freedom organisations have raised concerns over restrictions on journalists, internet blackouts and the use of force against demonstrators. Several news outlets were recently banned by Pakistan over their coverage of the crackdown by authorities in POJK.The Foreign Media Facilitation Guidelines, 2026 effectively place large parts of Pakistan beyond the reach of independent foreign reporting unless journalists first secure a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting’s External Publicity Wing (EP Wing). Until now, foreign correspondents could seek permissions on a case-by-case basis. The new framework formalises those controls and expands the government’s oversight over nearly every aspect of foreign media operations.Under the new rules, foreign journalists can freely operate only in Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi. Any reporting assignment elsewhere — including producing news reports, documentaries, videos or social media content — will require prior clearance from the government.International organisations, including Amnesty International and the Committee to Protect Journalists, have urged Pakistan to protect press freedom and investigate allegations of abuses.
. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 25 paise to end at 95 rupees and 13 paise against the US dollar.

. Young cyclist Harshita Jakhar rode into history books by becoming the first Indian woman to be a part of the Tour de France Femmes in Switzerland. The 19-year-old led a pack of eight talented cyclists from Afghanistan, Algeria, Chile, Ethiopia with two riders, Namibia and Uganda during the ceremonial start at Stage 2 of the gruelling race yesterday. The event started on 1st of this month in Lausanne and will end on 9th August in Nice.The team, handpicked by UCI (Union Cycliste de Internationale), cycled 4.5 kilometres on a neutralised section of the course along with some riders from the WCC Road Team.Tour de France Femmes is the women’s multi-stage cycling race that corresponds to the men’s Tour de France. It is part of the UCI Women’s World Tour calendar.UCI President David Lappartient joined the riders on the start podium before the stage and expressed his delight at seeing an Indian in the mix.Hailing from Rajasthan, Harshita has been making waves on the Indian cycling circuit, sweeping almost all the medals on offer in junior category and winning regularly in the seniors section as well. Her aim is to finish among the Top 10 at the 2026 Asian Games, and win a medal in the 2030 Games.

. Union Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has dedicated India’s first indigenous MA-104 Cell Line-Based Live Attenuated African Swine Fever (ASF) Vaccine for pigs. The Ministry said that the vaccine is a major breakthrough in veterinary research and is well suited for large-scale production. It said that the vaccine has successfully undergone comprehensive laboratory evaluation, including sterility, purity, safety, genetic stability, immunogenicity, protective efficacy and virulence reversion studies. The vaccine was field validated in collaboration with the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying further establishing its safety and efficacy under field conditions. The vaccine is recommended for healthy pigs above eight weeks of age and is administered as a 1 mL intramuscular injection, followed by a booster dose 14 days after the primary vaccination. Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Rajiv Ranjan Singh was present on the occasion.Speaking on the development, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education, Dr. M.L. Jat said that this breakthrough marks the dawn of a new era in veterinary science. He said that the breakthrough reflects India’s growing scientific capability to develop world-class animal health solutions and paves the way for a new generation of indigenously developed vaccines.Over 1.5 lakh passenger journeys were recorded in a single day on the Delhi-Meerut Namo Bharat on the 3rd of this month.

. The Government today said that it has strengthened the legal and institutional framework to deal with online piracy of cinematograph films, including unauthorized dissemination of films through intermediaries such as Telegram. In a written reply in Lok Sabha today, Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr. L Murugan said, the Cinematograph Act, 1952 was amended through the Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023 to introduce specific provisions to curb unauthorized recording and exhibition of films. The Minister also said that the newly inserted Section 7(1B)(ii) empowers the Government, under Section 79(3) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, to take action against intermediaries hosting pirated content. Mr. Murugan informed that under the Information Technology Rules, 2021, the intermediaries are required to remove any content violative of any law for the time being in force as and when brought to their knowledge either through a court order or through a notice by appropriate government or its authorized agency.

. Government has operationalized the Inventory-based Cross-border E-Commerce Export Framework under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023. The framework provides a comprehensive policy and procedural architecture for facilitating inventory-based cross-border e-commerce exports of goods manufactured or produced in India. It incorporates several safeguards to ensure that the benefits of e-commerce exports accrue to Indian manufacturers and MSMEs while maintaining regulatory oversight.The Framework also enables export-only inventory operations through registered exporters-on-record. It also provides for timely payments to Indian sellers within the prescribed timeline, irrespective of the receipt of payment from overseas buyers. Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the framework is expected to facilitate greater participation of Indian manufacturers, traders and MSMEs in global e-commerce supply chains by providing access to organized fulfillment networks while ensuring transparency, timely payments, effective pass-through of export benefits and robust regulatory oversight.

. In the Indian bullion market, 24 carat gold was trading 2.2 percent up at 1,47,490 rupees per 10 grams, while silver was trading three percent higher at 2,28,800 rupees per kilogram, a short while ago.On the Multi Commodity Exchange, Gold for the August contract was trading 1.8 percent up at 1,45,140 rupees per 10 grams and silver for the September contract was trading 2.7 percent up at 2,27,520 rupees per kilogram, when reports last came in.

. Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has achieved a 23.66 billion transaction count last month. In a social media post, the Department of Financial Services, under the Ministry of Finance, today thanked citizens for embracing digital payments and driving this revolution forward. It also called people to continue the journey of transforming the way the country transacts.

. The Government has refuted claims circulating on social media of fuel adulteration or contamination. In a social media post, the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas clarified that fuel quality is monitored on a regular basis by Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs). It said that in addition to the advanced and elaborate testing protocols already in place, further checks have been instituted, including water ingress testing about 8-12 times a day in over 87,000 outlets.The Ministry said that over two thousand samples have also been tested for chloride and sulphide, of which only 2 cases of chloride contamination have been found in the entire country till now, and sales from those pumps were suspended immediately. It said strict action will be taken in case any contamination or adulteration is found in any retail outlet. It informed that OMCs have also been instructed to take proactive steps to detect any possible contamination in the entire fuel supply chain.

. Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi held a meeting with senior officials of the Education Ministry to review ongoing initiatives and discuss key priorities for strengthening India’s education sector.In a social media post, Mr Joshi said, during the meeting, they deliberated on measures to enhance the quality, accessibility and inclusiveness of education while accelerating the effective implementation of flagship programmes.The Minister also reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to building a future-ready education ecosystem that empowers every learner and contributes to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

. NASA, the US space agency, has announced that the second stage of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket crashed into the Moon’s surface early today. The impact occurred at 12:05 PM IST.The Falcon 9 rocket was launched on January 15, 2025, carrying two commercial robotic lunar landers. After completing its mission, the rocket’s first stage successfully returned to Earth, while the second stage was left in space to drift.According to scientists, the impact created a crater measuring approximately 20 to 30 metres in diameter on the lunar surface.Researchers said the rare event, an artificial object striking the Moon, provided valuable scientific data, offering new insights into the Moon’s surface and helping improve planning for future lunar exploration missions.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has said, India stands for inclusive, demand-driven development cooperation with Africa that enhances local capacity to support national priorities.Speaking on the occasion of Africa Day in New Delhi yesterday, Dr Jaishankar noted that India is proud to be one of Africa’s largest trade and investment partners and the bilateral trade between the two nations stood at 93 billion last year. He added that India has also emerged as one of the top investors in Africa, with cumulative investments exceeding 80 billion dollar.Dr Jaishankar said, India’s approach to Africa is guided by the ten principles outlined by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his address to the Ugandan Parliament in 2018. He added these principles enshrine Africa among the top priorities of India with engagements through demand driven development partnerships, open markets for trade and investment, digital revolution for Africa’s development.The External Affairs Minister stressed that India’s enduring commitment to the Global South and the African Continent is reflected in the inclusion of the African Union as a permanent member of G20 during India’s presidency.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya today felicitated Indian athletes who returned from the Commonwealth Games 2026 after delivering historic performances in boxing, judo and para-athletics. During the felicitation ceremony held in New Delhi, the medal winners were presented cash awards of 30 lakh rupees for gold, 20 lakh rupees for silver and 10 lakh rupees for bronze.Interacting with the athletes, Dr. Mandaviya asked the athletes to think beyond their playing careers and become contributors to the next generation of Indian sport. The Minister highlighted the revamped Khelo India scheme of worth rupees 36,000 crore. He said that this initiative will take care of greater continued investment in the growth of Indian sports in the coming years. Congratulating the champions, Dr. Mandaviya urged them to extend their contribution to Indian sport beyond their competitive careers by mentoring and inspiring the next generation of athletes.

. Former champion PV Sindhu will be the ninth seed in the women’s singles event at the BWF World Badminton Championships 2026, scheduled to be held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in New Delhi from August 17 to 23. India’s highest-seeded entry at the World Badminton Championships will be the men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who have been handed the fifth seed. Former world championships bronze medallist Lakshya Sen is seeded 14th in men’s singles, while Dhruv Kapila and Olympian Tanisha Crasto are the 15th seeds in mixed doubles. India will have two entries in each of the five badminton disciplines at the home world championships, with at least one seeded contender in four of them.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met the Co-CEO of Netflix, Ted Sarandos in New Delhi. The Prime Minister said in a social media post that India has a rich tradition of storytelling and an extraordinary pool of creative talent, which can be leveraged to strengthen the country’s position as a global hub for content creation. Mr Modi said that they discussed the immense potential of India’s media and entertainment sector.Meanwhile, Netflix India has said the two leaders discussed their shared vision of taking India’s media and entertainment industry to the global stage. The streaming platform also announced the launch of the Netflix India Storytelling Initiative, an investment aimed at nurturing the next generation of India’s creative talent through skilling and education partnerships with the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) and the National Film Development Corporation.

. Global crude oil prices rose today. Brent crude was trading 1.4 per cent up at 80 US dollars and 45 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.8 per cent higher at 76 US dollars and 37 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. Minister of Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that cinema is more than entertainment; it is a bridge to culture, heritage and tourism. He said this during a fireside chat with Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat highlighted that every Indian story has the potential to inspire someone, somewhere in the world, to experience India. The Minister said that India’s ancient civilisation and cultural diversity are its greatest strengths, and platforms like Netflix can play a key role in taking India’s stories and soft power to global audiences. He noted that the ministry’s partnership with Netflix, including the As Seen on Netflix integration on the Incredible India portal, reflects the shared vision of showcasing India’s rich cultural diversity and strengthening its global soft power through authentic storytelling. Mr Shekhawat also stressed that the Centre is working with all stakeholders to provide tourists with a seamless travel experience across the country.On the sidelines of the fireside chat, talking to Akashvani News, Mr  Shekhawat said that the Ministry’s partnerships with platforms such as Netflix, YouTube, Google, and airline companies including IndiGo and Air India are based on non-commercial and mutually beneficial agreements, without financial payments by the government to these companies.He said that these collaborations will promote India’s tourism globally by showcasing the country’s destinations and cultural diversity. The Minister highlighted that visual storytelling plays a crucial role in influencing travellers’ decisions.

. The Government has said that the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) administered by the Department of Consumer Affairs has emerged as a single point of access to consumers across the country for their grievance redressal at a pre-litigation stage. In a written reply in Lok Sabha today, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution B L Verma said that consumers can register their grievances from all over the country in 17 languages through a toll-free number 1915.The Minister also said that 1,853 companies, who have voluntarily partnered with NCH, as part of the ‘Convergence’ programme directly respond to these grievances according to their redressal process and revert by providing a feedback to the complainant on the portal. Mr Verma also informed that NCH has successfully facilitated refunds amounting to over 91 crore rupees (including over 63 Crore rupees with regard to the grievances pertaining to e-commerce sector) to consumers between 25th April 2025 and 30th June 2026 by effectively addressing over 1,47,000 consumer grievances related to refund claims at the pre-litigation stage.

. Students intensified their protest over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand. Ahead of the monsoon session of the state assembly, set to begin today, five protesters, including two women, joined Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on a hunger strike for the past four days. Mahto’s health became a matter of concern after his blood sugar and pressure levels dropped significantly.Chief Minister Hemant Soren yesterday asserted that his government was committed to solving students’ problems. In a post on social media, he said, his government is working on this matter with complete seriousness. He said, the agencies are conducting investigations day and night, and the culprits are being sent to jail, he said.The protest began on July 25 under the banner of the JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium in Ranchi. The protesters said they had been forced to adopt the extreme form of agitation after repeated appeals to the government failed to produce any concrete action.The demonstrators are demanding cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand PSC Civil Services Examination and an independent probe into the alleged irregularities in the recruitment test either by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or by a panel of retired high court judges from outside the state. They also stressed comprehensive reforms in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC).

. The 2026 Commonwealth Games will come to a close with a spectacular closing ceremony at the iconic Hydro Arena in Glasgow tonight. The ceremony will begin at 1:30 am Indian Standard Time and will celebrate eleven days of sporting excellence, friendship and cultural diversity. On the occasion, Ahmedabad will receive the Commonwealth Games flag and the Host Baton in a ceremonial handover during the closing ceremony, marking India as the host for the centenary 2030 edition.India’s impressive campaign at the Games, highlighted by a record-breaking performance in boxing, historic success in judo, milestone achievements in para sports and multiple medals in athletics, propelled the country to fourth place in the overall medal standings with 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze medals.The closing ceremony at Glasgow’s famous Hydro arena, which holds up to 13,000 fans, will bring eleven days of athletic competition to a finale. The event, which is primarily a celebration of athlete performances, also acts as a thank you to the numerous volunteers and presents the hosts for the last time with performances by cultural organizations and community groups. The official transfer to the 24th Commonwealth Games in Amdavad in 2030 will also take place during the event.The event will be headlined by Scottish rock band Simple Minds. BEMZ, Cammy Barnes and Sandi Thom will also perform, while Australian singer Delta Goodrem will be making her third appearance at a Commonwealth Games ceremony. From India, Rashmika Mandanna and Shankar Mahadevan will headline India’s cultural showcase in Glasgow. Doordarshan will broadcast the ceremony LIVE for the fans.

. In the Asian markets, South Korea’s Kospi index rose around 3.8 per cent, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained nearly 3.7 per cent. Major European indices were trading on a mixed note today. Germany’s DAX added 0.3 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 dropped by 0.2 per cent, when reports last came in.

. Ministry of Consumers Affairs, Food and Public Distribution has invited applications from qualified polytechnics, ITIs, engineering colleges and testing units for getting accredited as Government Approved Test Centres (GATCs) under the Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013. The Ministry has noted that the application for the accreditation can be submitted online through the Department’s official portal from 17th to 31st of this month. It said the fully digital portal can be used efficiently for weights and measures by increasing the participation of technically competent private institutions. The ministry has informed that the licensing initiative is aimed at expanding India’s verification ecosystem for weights and measures by increasing the participation of technically competent private institutions.

. The Met Department has informed that heavy rain will continue in all districts in Keralam today and tomorrow. Orange Alert, indicating isolated very heavy rainfall, has been issued for Kasaragod, Kannur, Idukki, Ernakulam, Kottayam, Alappuzha, and Pathanamthitta districts today. Yellow Alert predicting isolated heavy rainfall is in place for all other seven districts. Places including Kakkanad, Kumarakom, and Alappuzha have been experiencing up to 15 mm of rain since 4:00 AM today.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended on a positive note today. The Sensex gained 152 points  to close at 78,581. The Nifty rose marginally by 10 points to settle at 24,625.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index rose 0.2 per cent, and the Smallcap 100 index added 0.8 per cent.Earlier, the markets opened in the positive zone, but as the session progressed, both benchmark indices slipped into negative territory. However, towards the end of the session, the Sensex and the Nifty pared losses after the closing auction session.In the Sensex pack, 18 out of 30 companies registered gains. Among the top gainers, Ultratech Cement rose two per cent, NTPC increased 1.8 per cent and State Bank of India as well as Mahindra and Mahindra added 1.7 per cent. In contrast, Tata consultancy services lost 1.2 per cent, HCL Tech shed 1.1 per cent and Reliance fell 0.9 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 21 out of 28 sectors ended in the positive zone. Among the top gainers, Housing Finance advanced 1.8 per cent, Metal rose 1.6 per cent and Auto gained 1.4 per cent. In contrast, Mid-small Private Banks Quality Tilt, Energy and Oil and Gas fell by 0.4 per cent, Mid-small Private Banks fell 0.3 per cent and  Capital Goods dropped by 0.2 per centThe overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2292 companies advanced, 1958 declined and 198 remained unchanged.

. Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh today emphasized that technology and tradition must progress together to ensure the long term growth of the handloom sector.Addressing the inaugural ceremony of Centre of Excellence in Handloom Technology at Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi, the Minister said that this center will play a pivotal role in bridging traditional crafts and modern technology, enhancing weavers’ productivity, promoting innovation and connecting their products to new markets. He added that the center will support research, skill development and innovation, enabling artisans and weavers to adopt modern techniques without compromising India’s rich weaving heritage. The Minister further underlined the need to develop new and sustainable fibres to meet changing consumer preferences and strengthen the handloom sector.On the occasion, Mr Singh also launched five flagship initiatives, including handloom 4.0, handloom x, handloom e-vidya, Kalagriha handloom studio and Threads of Valour.

. Union Minister for Development of the North Eastern Region, Jyotiraditya Scindia, today met Commonwealth Games gold medallist Mirabai Chanu in New Delhi and congratulated her on winning a record-extending third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal in Glasgow. During the meeting, Mr Scindia lauded Mirabai Chanu’s determination and perseverance, and noted that her achievement will inspire young athletes across the country, particularly in the Northeast. They also discussed various aspects of high-performance sports, including training, nutrition, recovery and athlete support.The Minister highlighted the Centre’s efforts to strengthen the sporting ecosystem in the Northeast through the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region’s High-Level Task Force and the One State, One Sport initiative. He said that the primary focus of the Government is to create world-class coaching, scientific training and sports infrastructure, nurturing more champions from the region.

. Union Minister J P Nadda has said the scale of devastation by the latest wave of floods in Assam was so enormous that it will take time to restore normalcy.Deputed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Union Health and Family Welfare Minister toured Nepalikhuti area of Sivasagar district along the Assam-Nagaland border, which is one of the worst-hit regions in the latest wave of floods that struck on July 19. The Union minister, along with the CM, visited flood-affected areas of Nazira, where he went to the relief camps, agricultural fields and residential areas.The flood situation in Assam has worsened, with the toll rising to 95 with six more deaths, and the number of affected increasing to 1.6 lakh across 14 districts.In the evening, he held a high-level review meeting with Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma. He assured the affected people of all possible assistance from the Centre, including financial aid, rehabilitation and compensation. He said the PM had deputed him to assess the ground situation and that he had discussed the impact of the floods in detail with the chief minister. He also received detailed information from local residents regarding the flood situation, losses incurred and reconstruction requirements.

. At the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, India’s medal hunt enters the final day with judo and track cycling offering the last opportunities to add to the tally. Avtar Singh in the men’s 100kg, Yash Ghangas in the men’s +100kg and Ishroop Narang in the women’s 78kg category will lead India’s judo challenge, while Ronaldo Laitonjam will compete in the men’s 1,000-metre time trial in track cycling. Para track cycling events are also scheduled on the closing day.India climbed to fourth place in the Commonwealth Games 2026 medal standings in Glasgow following a remarkable Day 10, securing 16 medals on Saturday. This surge brought India’s tally to 39 medals, comprising 13 gold, 17 silver, and 9 bronze, with the boxing contingent leading the charge.India finished atop the boxing medal table, achieving its best-ever performance at the Commonwealth Games with a record seven gold and three silver medals. Among the gold medallists, Ankush Panghal defeated England’s Dimeji Shittu 4-1 in the men’s 80kg final, while Sachin Siwach edged past Namibia’s Tryagain Morning Ndevelo 3-2 to claim the men’s 60kg title. The other Indian boxing gold medallists included Jaismine Lamboria, Preeti Pawar, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, and Arundhati Choudhary.Three Indian boxers, Narender Berwal, Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, and Jadumani Singh, settled for silver medals. Narender lost to England’s Damar Thomas by a unanimous decision in the men’s 90+kg final. Lovlina went down 4-1 to Australia’s Emma-Sue Greentree in the women’s 75kg final. Preeti claimed the women’s 54-kilogram boxing title with a commanding 5-0 victory over Canada’s Scarlett Delgado. Jaismine, the reigning world champion, secured another 5-0 win in the women’s 57-kilogram final, defeating Michaela Walsh of Northern Ireland.Sakshi then beat Ruby White of England in the women’s 51-kilogram final 5-0 to win. It was a harder final bout for Priya, who beat Marie-Bathoul Al-Ahmadieh of Canada 4-1 in a split verdict in the women’s 60-kilogram final. Arundhati Choudhary also defeated Chantelle Reid of England in the women’s 70-kilogram final.Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh has scripted history at the Commonwealth Games, winning bronze in the men’s 5,000 metres after a silver in the 10,000 metres. He becomes the first Indian track and field athlete to win two medals in a single edition of the Games and the first Indian to claim a Commonwealth medal in the 5,000 metres. The reigning Asian champion clocked 13 minutes 24.95 seconds to complete a historic double.India also celebrated a historic achievement in para-athletics, with Soman Rana winning gold and Shubham Juyal taking silver in the men’s shot put F57 event. This result marked India’s first-ever Commonwealth Games gold medal in the men’s shot put F57 event and the nation’s first double podium finish in the category.In the men’s triple jump event, Praveen Chithravel won silver, while Selva Prabhu Thirumaran clinched bronze. On the judo mat, Unnati Sharma clinched the women’s 63kg bronze medal after defeating Skye Knoester of South Africa by Ippon in the third-place contest. Karanjit Singh Maan reached the men’s -90kg quarter-finals with an ippon win over New Zealand’s Elliott Connolly before suffering defeats to Canada’s Guillaume Gaulin in the last eight and Scotland’s Scott Cuscak in the repechage.

. Arunachal’s para shuttler Biri Takar has clinched Double Medal at BWF Para World Circuit in Brazil. Takar has won Gold in Men’s Doubles and Bronze in Men’s Singles. Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu congratulated the sportsman for his international achievements.Congratulating the athlete, Chief Minister in a social media post highlighted that Takar is a beneficiary of the Chief Minister’s Award to Champion Excellence in Sports (CM ACES) programme.  and said his international success reflects the programme growing impact on nurturing sporting talent in the state.

. Indian Railways has approved modifications in the Model Concession Agreement. Under this, Container Train Operators, or CTOs, will now be permitted to run container trains on all routes across the Indian Railways network under a single All India licence, with a uniform registration fee of 25 crore rupees. The government has also removed the earlier system of separate permissions and fees for different route categories.The Ministry further informed that the approved amendments provide that the permission granted to a Container Train Operator may be extended for a further period of 20 years after its expiry.The Ministry said the uniform registration fee and removal of extension fees are expected to reduce regulatory costs and simplify the approval process, encouraging greater private participation and expansion of container train operations. It added that a higher shift of container traffic from road to rail will help ease highway congestion, reduce fuel consumption and carbon emissions, and promote sustainable freight transportation. The approved amendments also provide for the extension of a Container Train Operator’s permission for a further period of 20 years after its expiry.

Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal met Uzbekistan’s Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade Laziz Kudratov in New Delhi today.  In a social media post, Mr Goyal said that during their meeting, they had productive discussions on further strengthening the India-Uzbekistan Strategic Partnership by enhancing cooperation in trade, investment, pharmaceuticals, connectivity, digital technologies and manufacturing. Mr Goyal expressed confidence that the growing partnership between the two nations will unlock new opportunities for businesses and contribute to shared prosperity.

. The Ministry of Education today opened the online registration portal for Yuva Sangam Phase VII under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat initiative. The Ministry said that interested youth aged between 18 and 30 years, including students of Higher Education Institutions, NSS/NYKS volunteers, and young professionals, are eligible to register. It said that for Phase VII, 20 Higher Education Institutions including IITs, IIMs, Central Universities and NITs have been identified as nodal institutions to host and facilitate the exchange programme. Selected participants will undertake five to seven day educational and cultural tours to their paired States and Union Territories. They will gain first-hand exposure to local traditions, educational institutions, governance initiatives, innovation ecosystems, industries, heritage sites, and community life during the exchange programme.
